key_insight: CARing improves next-visit diagnosis prediction by pairing compact medical token representations with a coverage-based reward so the model learns to cover multiple valid diagnoses, not just repeat a few easy ones.
clinical_relevance: This could help clinical NLP systems produce more complete differential diagnosis predictions from longitudinal EHRs, especially in multi-label settings where several diagnoses may be correct at once.
method: Represents diagnoses as compact Semantic IDs (SIDs) learned from ontology-enriched disease semantics via residual quantization.
Aligns SID tokens with natural language and EHR context using multi-task alignment and reasoning-enriched training.
Uses coverage reward plus multi-positive supervision, with direct constrained decoding or multi-chain reasoning at inference.
evidence_signal: On MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV, the method outperformed EHR-trained baselines in weighted F1 and achieved the best top-k recall at all reported cutoffs, including R@30 of 46.04% and 46.52% in reasoning mode.
watch_item: Because the approach depends on learned SID vocabularies, constrained decoding, and EHR-specific training data, performance may be sensitive to ontology quality and integration into real clinical workflows.
paper_title: Coverage-Aware Reasoning with Medical Tokens for Diagnosis Prediction
